nodes.name: FeCoNiCu MEA NP synthesis
nodes.procedure: FeCoNiCu NPs were synthesized through a nonequilibrium wet-chemical co-reduction approach. A precursor mixture [of Fe, Co, Ni, Cu precursors] was injected into oleylamine with a borane morpholine complex at 260°C and maintained for 30 min. The nanoparticle powder was collected by a repeated centrifugation and washing process (see details in the Supporting Information).

nodes.description: OER LSV performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The OER performance of MEA NPs was evaluated in 1 M KOH along with Pd NPs (XRD and TEM in Figures S8 and S9). The linear sweep voltammogram (LSV) curves normalized by the geometric area of the electrode are shown in Figure 3a... Pd-FeCoNiCu displayed the lowest overpotentials (225.32 ± 0.38 mV @ 10 mA cm−2 and 266.97 ± 0.93 mV @ 100 mA cm−2... The Tafel slope of Pd-FeCoNiCu was 40.36 ± 0.43 mVdec−1... double-layer capacitance (Cdl) was employed... Pd-FeCoNiCu possessed the largest Cdl value of 7.98±0.14 mFcm−2... The Faradaic efficiency (FE) of Pd-FeCoNiCu at 10 mA cm−2 was 98.80±1.89%... at 100 mA cm−2, which likely relates to metal dissolution at a high current density.

nodes.description: OER accelerating durability test ADT at 100 mA/cm2
nodes.source_text: In an accelerating durability test (ADT) at 100 mA cm−2, it exhibits a mere 8.9 mV increase over 25 h with a degradation rate of 0.356 mV h−1... at a large current density of 100 mA cm−2, Pd-FeCoNiCu exhibited only an 8.9 mV increase during a 25 h stability test... Pd-FeCoNiCu exhibits a degradation rate of only 0.36 mV h−1 at 100 mA cm−2.

nodes.description: OER long-term stability CP at 10 mA/cm2
nodes.source_text: The stability of MEANPs was evaluated by the CP method. The activity can be maintained for 1000 h at 10 mA cm−2 without a notable decay (Figure S13), while Pd NPs and FeCoNiCu can only sustain 2 and 10 h, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and HAADF-STEM reveal Pd-FeCoNiCu average size 6.4(3) nm with no oxidation layer; FeCoNiCu average size 9.0(2) nm with ~2 nm surface oxidized layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Bright-field transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images reveal that the average sizes of FeCoNiCu and Pd-FeCoNiCu are 9.0(2) nm and 6.4(3) nm, respectively (Figures 1a, S1, and S2). The FeCoNiCu NPs exhibit a discernible surface oxidized layer of approximately 2 nm (Figure S1). Conversely, no oxidation layer appears in Pd-FeCoNiCu (Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM confirms atomic-level Pd dilution in FeCoNiCu matrix with no surface Pd aggregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM images reveal brighter Pd atoms encircled in white within atom columns, confirming atomic-level Pd dilution in the FeCoNiCu matrix ... No surface aggregation of Pd is observed in Pd-FeCoNiCu.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS shows homogeneous elemental distribution of Fe, Co, Ni, Cu in both catalysts with no elemental segregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STEM-energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) data indicated no elemental segregation, confirming the homogeneous distribution of each element in the MEA host.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pd-FeCoNiCu composition confirmed as Fe: 7.50(3)%, Co: 27.86(4)%, Ni: 29.32(4)%, Cu: 35.12(4)%, Pd: 0.31(1)% by ICP-OES.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-OES was employed to confirm the definitive atomic ratios ... The atomic ratios were Fe: 7.50(3)%, Co: 27.86(4)%, Ni: 29.32(4)%, Cu: 35.12(4)%, and Pd: 0.31(1)%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Both Pd-FeCoNiCu and FeCoNiCu MEA NPs exhibit face-centered-cubic (fcc) structure similar to Cu/Pd metal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns reveal that both MEA NPs exhibit a face-centered-cubic (fcc) structure, akin to that of Cu/Pd metal.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pd K-edge XANES shows metallic Pd (overlaps Pd foil); Fe K-edge indicates mainly +3 oxidation state; Co/Ni show mixed (hydro)oxide/metallic states; Cu mainly metallic. Difference spectra show decreased pre-edge d-DOS, weakened antibonding states, and more complex multiscattering in Pd-FeCoNiCu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XANES of the Pd K-edge ... exhibited an absorption edge that almost overlaps with that of Pd foil ... The Fe K-edge in Pd-FeCoNiCu indicated Fe mainly in a +3-oxidation state ... Weak pre-edge features at the Co and Ni K-edges suggest the co-presence of (hydro)Co/Ni oxidation states and metallic states, while Cu was mainly in a metallic state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pd 3d peaks at 335.7 eV (3d5/2) and 340.0 eV (3d3/2) confirm metallic Pd unchanged after 1h ADT at 100 mA cm⁻²; degree of oxidation after ADT reduced by 81.3% (Fe), 91.7% (Co), 84.4% (Ni), 53.3% (Cu) vs FeCoNiCu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Pd 3d spectra, the peaks located at 335.7 and 340.0 eV were respectively attributed to 3d5/2 and 3d3/2 of metallic Pd ... The Pd 3d peak position remained unchanged after the OER ... For Fe, Co, Ni, and Cu, the degree of oxidation is 81.3%, 91.7%, 84.4%, and 53.3% less, respectively, than that of FeCoNiCu.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pd K-edge FT-EXAFS shows single main peak at 2.2 Å from Pd-M bonds (M=Fe,Co,Ni,Cu) instead of Pd-Pd at 2.5 Å, confirming isolated Pd atoms surrounded by Fe/Co/Ni/Cu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Pd K-edge (Figure 2b), Pd-FeCoNiCu exhibited only one main peak at 2.2 Å, contributed by Pd-M (M=Fe, Co, Ni, Cu) instead of Pd-Pd (at 2.5 Å in the Pd foil).
